title: The Open Trail
premise: Desert ranger Coral Joubert has spent three years chasing the man who stole her brother's water rights and left him to die, moving from one empty range to the next because grief is easier than stillness. When a government survey team vanishes in the high country — gear intact, no tracks, permits expiring with the first snows — Coral is conscripted to find them and discovers the thief she's hunted is already there, working as the team's guide. Trapped together by weather and a conspiracy to falsify land claims that would strip the desert's last free water, Coral must choose between the justice she planned and the survival of strangers. She crosses the range ahead of the snows carrying evidence instead of a gun, delivers it to a federal judge, and finally stops moving — burying her brother's memory where he wanted to be buried.
about_author: Elodie Amberdale is the pen name of a former backcountry surveyor who spent a decade mapping arid ranges across the American Southwest before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for spare prose, unforgiving landscapes, and protagonists who mistake endurance for peace.

chapters.title: Salt Flat Morning
chapters.summary: Coral tracks a petty horse thief across cracked alkali flats, catching him in hours but lingering days after, unable to ride home. Third-person limited POV establishes her restlessness and the ranger code she lives by: keep moving, want nothing. Emotional beat: competence masking emptiness.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: In the town of Dry Wells, Coral rereads her brother Tomas's stolen water ledger for the hundredth time, hunting the signature of Renn Calloway, the broker who erased his claim. A telegram arrives: a federal survey team has gone missing in the Vermilion Range. POV: Coral. Beat: old wound reopened by duty.

chapters.title: Conscripted
chapters.summary: The territorial marshal deputizes Coral against her will — she knows the high passes better than anyone alive. She argues, loses, and rides north with a week of supplies and no desire to find anyone alive. POV: Coral. Beat: resentment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral reaches the abandoned survey camp: tents pitched, instruments wrapped, food cached, six people gone without a single footprint. The wrongness unsettles her professional certainty. POV: Coral. Beat: dread replacing boredom; the mystery becomes personal craft-pride.

chapters.title: A Familiar Boot Print
chapters.summary: Among the scattered tracks Coral finds a boot heel scarred by a farrier's mistake she'd recognize anywhere — Renn Calloway's. He was guiding the survey team when they vanished. POV: Coral. Beat: the hunt and the mission fuse into one obsession.

chapters.title: The Widow of Pine Hollow
chapters.summary: Coral finds the sole survivor, surveyor Ada Quist, half-frozen in a mine adit. Ada speaks in fragments about men who came at night wearing concession badges. POV alternates Coral and Ada. Beat: fragile trust between two women who owe each other nothing.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Ada reveals the team discovered the aquifer maps were forged — the water rights sold to Calloway's syndicate sit on dry rock, while real water runs under unclaimed land the syndicate wants cleared. POV: Ada. Beat: the theft Coral chased is one thread of something vast.

chapters.title: Six Went Up
chapters.summary: Ada recounts the night the badged men took the other five surveyors toward the old Consolidated mine. Coral calculates: storm front three days out, mine a day's climb, permits expire Friday. POV: Coral. Beat: the clock starts; hesitation now costs lives.

chapters.title: Switchbacks
chapters.summary: Coral and Ada climb into thinning air, Ada slowing them, Coral fighting the urge to leave her behind. A near-fall on scree forces Coral to catch her and admit, silently, that she can't carry another death. POV: Coral. Beat: reluctant interdependence.

chapters.title: The Man at the Fire
chapters.summary: At timberline they find a burning camp and Renn Calloway sitting beside it, hands visible, rifle unloaded. He says he ran when the badged men came, and that he's been trying to undo what he did to Tomas. POV: Coral. Beat: rage meeting an enemy who won't perform villainy.

chapters.title: Three Years of Nothing
chapters.summary: By firelight, Calloway confesses: he forged the ledger entries under orders, then kept running from Coral's pursuit because confession meant naming the syndicate's principals. He offers names if she gets him off the mountain. POV: Coral. Beat: vengeance curdling into negotiation; nothing feels clean.

chapters.title: Snow Line
chapters.summary: The first snow arrives early, erasing their back-trail and any retreat. They shelter in a prospector's cabin where Coral reads Tomas's last letter aloud for the first time in years. POV: Coral. Beat: grief thawing; the price of survival counted in honesty.

chapters.title: Badges in the Drift
chapters.summary: Two syndicate riders find the cabin. In a tense standoff, Coral talks them into believing the survivors died in the snow — then follows their tracks down toward the Consolidated mine. POV: Coral. Beat: Coral discovers she can win with words, unsettling everything she believes about herself.

chapters.title: The Consolidated
chapters.summary: They reach the mine and find the five surveyors alive, held as leverage until the permits lapse and the land reverts. The foreman, Vess, offers Coral a cut to walk away. POV: Coral. Beat: temptation made concrete and insultingly small.

chapters.title: Counting Heads
chapters.summary: Coral scouts the mine's single shaft entrance, counting guards, mapping collapse timbers, weighing eleven lives against speed. Calloway volunteers a plan that requires trusting him completely. POV: Calloway. Beat: the hunted man asking to be useful; Coral's silence as consent.

chapters.title: Blown Timber
chapters.summary: Calloway collapses a support to seal the guards inside the lower workings while Coral leads the surveyors up the ventilation raise. A guard grabs Ada; Coral makes a choice she'll carry forever. POV: Coral. Beat: survival exacting its price in blood and guilt.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Above treeline the storm closes fully. Eleven people rope together in zero visibility, Coral navigating by memory and braille of wind, Calloway breaking trail until his hands stop working. POV: Coral. Beat: the whole book compressed into one crossing — movement as meaning.

chapters.title: The Ledge
chapters.summary: A cornice fails; Calloway goes over and hangs by Coral's rope. She holds him, the man who killed her brother's future, and hauls him up because letting go would cost more than holding on. POV: Coral. Beat: climax of theme — justice cannot be administered by gravity.

chapters.title: Permit Expiry
chapters.summary: They descend into Dry Wells on the morning the permits lapse, Coral walking straight into the land office with Ada's testimony, the forged maps, and Calloway's sworn statement naming the syndicate. POV: Coral. Beat: law reclaimed from the lawless; the trail ends at a desk.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Before the federal judge, Calloway testifies and is taken into custody; the syndicate's principals are named and warrants issued. Coral refuses reward money, asking instead that the aquifer stay unclaimed commons. POV: Coral. Beat: justice outside her own hands, and finding it sufficient.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Coral stays in Dry Wells through the thaw, repairing fences, teaching Ada to read contour lines, discovering that stillness hurts less than she feared. POV: Coral. Beat: quiet reckoning; the price of survival paid, the change surviving it.

chapters.title: The Open Trail
chapters.summary: Spring. Coral rides to the ridge where Tomas asked to have his ashes spread, does it at last, and speaks his name into the wind. Then she turns her horse not away from home but toward it. POV: Coral. Beat: resolution — the open trail remains, but so does the door.
